## Context
During the comment-remediation epic, Gerrit briefly advertised `main` with parent `0fe2cc2e…` while Gitiles returned 404 for that object. Ref history appeared rewound and omitted merged commit `2a93f180…`. `git fetch gerrit main` returned timeout/HTTP 504, and CI run `34235734839` failed checkout when Gerrit returned HTTP 502 fetching change 2834. The service later recovered: the parent became readable and ref advertisement worked again.

This ticket owns the `/rebar-debug` investigation requested by the operator. RCA confirmed the actionable failure class: the pinned `checkout-gerrit-change-action` is mirror-first only when the GitHub mirror exposes the requested Gerrit change ref. Run 34235734839 showed GitHub lacked `refs/changes/34/2834/1`, forcing Gerrit fallback; the fallback returned HTTP 502 before repository validation. A later check found the ref visible on GitHub, proving the versioned refspec can work but that the live mirror can lag/miss until replication is triggered. The operator approved Option A: publish `refs/changes/*` to the org-private GitHub mirror and preserve the pinned action's mirror-first path.

## Plan
- Keep the existing main/tag/feature replication intact and update only the Gerrit change-ref replication spec to the operator-approved forced refspec `+refs/changes/*:refs/changes/*`, so updated change metadata and patchset refs are re-pushed during a full replication sweep without expanding to `refs/meta/*` or wildcard `refs/*`.
- Add/adjust a narrow repository test that parses `infra/gerrit/replication.config` and proves the remote `github` contains the exact `+refs/changes/*:refs/changes/*` refspec while retaining `refs/heads/main`, `refs/tags/*`, `refs/heads/feature/*`, `mirror = false`, `replicatePermissions = false`, and `projects = rebar`.
- Apply the repository config on the Gerrit host through the supported replication setup/materialization path, snapshotting the live `replication.config` first and using plugin reload if available; otherwise use the minimal documented Gerrit restart only if needed.
- Trigger full replication for remote `github` and monitor replication output/disk/CPU enough to catch obvious initial-load failures.
- Verify `refs/changes/*` visibility on GitHub with `git ls-remote`, spot-check an open change ref, and prove a CI-style `git fetch origin <refs/changes/...>` succeeds from the GitHub mirror without contacting Gerrit.
- Watch the first Mirror Guard run after the change and confirm it stays green with no replication-lag alarm.

## Testing
- RED: `pytest tests/scripts/test_gerrit_replication_config.py::<new refs_changes_refspec test>` fails before the config change because the file uses non-forced `refs/changes/*:refs/changes/*`.
- GREEN targeted: `pytest tests/scripts/test_gerrit_replication_config.py` plus `make config-check`.
- Final repository verification: `make verify PYTEST_WORKERS=2` with ambient GIT_CONFIG_* variables unset.
- Operational verification: after host apply and replication, `git ls-remote https://github.com/navapbc/rebar 'refs/changes/*'` returns change refs and a local fresh repo can `git fetch origin <open-change-ref>` from GitHub only.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The incident timeline is supported by exact Gerrit and CI evidence.
- [ ] A proven root cause explains the checkout 502/504: the mirror-first action fell back to Gerrit because the GitHub mirror lacked the requested change ref at validation time.
- [ ] The versioned Gerrit replication config publishes `+refs/changes/*:refs/changes/*` without disturbing main/tag/feature replication or refs/meta/config privacy controls.
- [ ] The live Gerrit host has the updated replication config applied and full replication has been triggered successfully.
- [ ] `refs/changes/*` visibility and a CI-style origin fetch are verified from the GitHub mirror without contacting Gerrit.
- [ ] Mirror Guard remains green after the change and no replication-lag alarm is observed.
